title: Organization-specific regression gates with local eval sandboxing
creator: Nina Rosen
description:
Problem: Customers running Dedicated or Private deployments require regression detection that respects their data boundaries and privacy controls. Our hosted evals are useful for public benchmarks but cannot safely run against customer proprietary corpora or in environments that prohibit telemetry export. Goal: Ship an org-specific regression gating capability that runs evaluation locally (inside customer VPC or an isolated sandbox container) and emits privacy-preserving telemetry (pass/fail signals, hashed summaries, and optional DP-noised metrics). The feature must integrate with Console rollouts so model/config changes can be blocked or progressively rolled out based on customer-specific golden sets and thresholds.

Scope: prototype a lightweight local eval sandbox (EvalBox) that customers can opt into for Dedicated and Private tiers. EvalBox will: 1) execute pre-registered eval suites owned by the customer; 2) compare outputs to locally-stored golden examples using configurable metrics; 3) emit only agreed minimal telemetry (binary gate result, hashed summary, per-route token counts) to Redwood; 4) support selectable privacy modes (no-telemetry, aggregated, DP-noised summaries).

Non-goals: hosting or storing raw customer corpora in Redwood; full CI integration for arbitrary corpora (phase 2); replacing hosted eval pipeline for public models.
acceptance_criteria: EvalBox runs inside a customer VPC or isolated container and completes an org-specific eval suite without sending raw data to Redwood
Console exposes per-customer gate configuration: eval suite selection, metric thresholds, and privacy mode
When gate is enabled, Console rollout will block full rollout if EvalBox reports a failing gate for the target customer
Telemetry exported is limited to allowed artifacts (pass/fail, hashed 256-bit summary, small aggregated metrics) according to privacy mode
Pilot executed with 3 customers (two Dedicated, one Private on-prem) and regression detected in at least one intentional negative test
Security review completed and KMS/HSM integration documented for key management of local summaries
rollout_plan: Phase A (pilot): ship EvalBox alpha + Console gate UI to 3 beta customers; require manual opt-in and support from Solutions. Phase B: iterate on privacy modes and performance; add autoscaling for EvalBox runs and cost cap enforcement. Phase C: general availability for Dedicated and Private customers with self-serve opt-in and reporting in Console. Rollout will include customer training docs and runbooks for incident recovery.
metrics: Time-to-eval: median runtime per suite < 8 minutes for standard 500-example suite
False-positive gate rate during pilot < 5% (i.e., gate triggers incorrectly)
Telemetry size: average outbound telemetry per eval run < 4 KB in aggregated mode
Customer trust metric: pilot NPS >= 40 for feature usefulness and privacy satisfaction
comments: 2025-02-21 - Kickoff with Eng + Security + Solutions. Agreed primary privacy modes: no-telemetry, aggregated, DP-noised. Eng will prototype containerized EvalBox; Security requested key management design by next sync. (Attendees: Marco Delgado, Hannah Li, Priya Nair)

2025-02-26 - Engineering spike update: prototype can run suite in isolated container and emit a SHA256 hash of concatenated outputs. Perf note: first-run cold-start ~1.2x expected; caching of model artifacts inside EvalBox will be required. (Marco)

2025-03-01 - Product-design review: Console gate UI mockups reviewed; added explicit consent checkbox and audit log link per run. Priya suggested inline explanation of privacy modes and an escape hatch to force-continue rollout with org-approval.

2025-03-03 - Security feedback: require KMS integration for salt used in hashing and require signed attestation of EvalBox binary when running in customer on-prem. Added security_review_required flag. (Hannah)

2025-03-04 - Solution engineering note: incumbent customers asked for bulk-run capability and retention TTL controls. We'll add 'max-run-frequency' and 'local-retention-days' knobs in phase B. (Rita Chen)

2025-03-05 - Decision log: Proceed with pilot. Eng to ship alpha EvalBox image and CI for tests; PM to coordinate 3 pilot customers and create support runbooks. Metrics and acceptance criteria agreed.
